chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) that he said:
Regarding a man who sent his baggage (luggage) on the day of the first departure and stayed himself until the last, he said: 'He is among those who hastened [his departure] in two days.'

key_terms.الثَّقَل: Luggage or baggage of the pilgrim
key_terms.تَعَجَّلَ: Hastened (referring to the category of pilgrims who leave early)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّفْرِ الْأَخِيرِ: The day of the last departure (12th of Dhu al-Hijjah) during Hajj
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّفْرِ الْأَوَّلِ: The day of the first departure (11th of Dhu al-Hijjah) during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who sends their luggage back on the first day of Nafar but stays in Mina until the last day?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a pilgrim who opts for the 'hastened departure' (Nafar Awwal) by dispatching their luggage early while remaining in Mina for the final day. In Shia jurisprudence, this act is deemed sufficient to complete the requisite stay, thereby exempting the pilgrim from the penalty of staying beyond the prescribed time, illustrating the flexibility within the Hajj rituals. This ruling underscores the principle that the intention and partial fulfillment of the rite can suffice for legal completion, a key concept in Usul al-Fiqh regarding conditional obligations.
